secular-religious-08: State control over religious bodies does not establish whether they have an official advisory role in reviewing proposed laws; the question does not require independent review.
progressive-traditionalist-06: Civil Code marital fidelity and family virtues do not establish a societal preference for the specific two-parent married household over other family forms.
democracy-autocracy-14: Electoral Law articles 49–53 allow voters to petition for recall of county and township representatives, with a secret vote and majority of the original electorate required; qualified support reflects the local scope and Party-controlled institutions.
authority-liberty-13: Criminal procedure regulations articles 222–224 permit searches of homes with county-level police-chief approval and a police search warrant; prior court authorisation is not required even for ordinary non-emergency searches.
public-private-06: The state transferred national railway assets into a wholly state-owned corporation responsible for passenger transport and network construction; the 2019 successor retained state ownership. This supports public infrastructure without claiming every individual railway has exclusive public ownership.
public-private-08: The PBC 2025 stability report records six large state-owned commercial banks alongside nineteen private banks, and supports continued development of this differentiated banking system.
innovation-caution-08: The guidelines require sufficient evidence for invasive research and moderation for enhancement, but do not expressly define the proposed research-only restriction until strong long-term safety evidence. Section 5.4 specifically concerns non-invasive enhancement.
innovation-caution-11: General sections 3.2 and 4.1 require properly managed risks and sufficient safety-and-benefit evidence even for invasive research, supporting qualified rejection of access on basic safety alone. This normative inference does not treat the non-invasive enhancement section 5.4 as an implant-specific rule.
